newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Bucaram tries suing interim Ecuador president.
newsitem.headline: Bucaram tries suing interim Ecuador president.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed President Abdala Bucaram filed a petition with the Supreme Court on Wednesday asking it to start legal proceedings against interim President Fabian Alarcon for conspiracy.

Bucaram, who was dismissed by Ecuador's Congress last month for "mental incompetence" and is now living in Panama, sent a letter to Supreme Court President Carlos Solorzano demanding that Alarcon be jailed pending trial.

"We are going to present a private suit demanding jail for Alarcon in order to put things in order again and get Congress to restore the presidency to Abdala Bucaram," former prosecutor Leonidas Plaza told reporters.

In his letter to the Supreme Court, a copy of which was made available to Reuters, Bucaram said the "mental incapacity" charge levelled at him by Congress "has not been proved legally as the Constitution requires" by medical experts.

Bucaram was ousted after six months in power in a wave of popular protest and strikes against his tough economic reforms and eccentric personal style. His stunts included singing in a rock band and lunch with Lorena Bobbit, the Ecuadorean-born American famous for slicing off her husband's penis.

The government of Alarcon, named interim president until 1998, has filed suits against Bucaram for alleged mishandling and illegal appropriation of public funds. The military has declared him "persona non grata" and plans to sue him for "insulting the honour" of the forces and the country.
Bucaram continues to call himself president from exile in Panama, where he lived from 1985-90 after he fleeing charges of corruption as mayor of his home city Guayaquil.
